name: Oahu
why: The North Shore's Pipeline, Sunset Beach and Waimea Bay are the most famous winter waves on Earth, for experts only. In summer the south shore, including Waikiki, has gentle, beginner-friendly waves, so the island works for every level in the right season. Best: North Shore Nov–Feb (expert only); south shore and Waikiki in summer. (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the surfing list in the old Catalog Wishlist (not yet imported).

name: Southern California
why: Lower Trestles near San Clemente, Huntington Beach ("Surf City"), Malibu and Rincon near Ventura form the densest cluster of quality waves in the continental US, with water warm enough for a spring suit in summer. Monterey & Big Sur, the nearest catalog place, is cold, central-California surf. Best: Year-round; summer south swell, winter northwest swell. (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the surfing list in the old Catalog Wishlist (not yet imported).
grainNote: A long coast (San Diego to Santa Barbara), but one trip.

name: Hossegor & the Landes Coast
why: La Gravière, La Nord and the other sandbar beach breaks make this Europe's best-known beach-break coast and a long-time world tour stop. Basque Country (Mundaka), the nearest catalog place, is a very different wave. Best: Sep–Nov (October most often cleanest); summer gentle, winter big. (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the surfing list in the old Catalog Wishlist (not yet imported).

name: Mentawai Islands
why: Lance's Right, Macaronis and other reef passes are among the world's best waves, reached by live-aboard boat charters. A very different offer from Bali's day-trip reefs. Best: About Apr–Oct (the dry-season swell). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the surfing list in the old Catalog Wishlist (not yet imported).
grainNote: An island group, one boat trip.

name: Jeffreys Bay
why: Supertubes is one of the best right-hand point breaks on Earth and a regular world tour event. It is about a 7-hour drive from Cape Town, a separate trip from Muizenberg's beginner waves. Best: Jun–Aug (June most often cleanest); roughly Apr–Sep. (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Named in the Cape Town text as a separate trip.
grainNote: Slightly specific: one town, though its coast runs west.

name: Gold Coast & Byron Bay
why: Snapper Rocks and the Superbank run for hundreds of meters, with Kirra, Burleigh Heads and Byron's The Pass nearby. Sydney, the nearest catalog place, is a very different, urban surf. Best: About Feb–Jun (cyclone and autumn swell). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.)

name: Margaret River
why: Main Break, The Box and Surfers Point are heavy reef and point waves on a wine-region coast. A long way from any other catalog place. Best: About Apr–Oct (autumn the standout). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the surfing list in the old Catalog Wishlist (not yet imported).
grainNote: A coastline and its town, one trip.

name: Chicama & Máncora
why: Chicama is famous as one of the longest left-hand waves in the world, with rides that can last minutes. Máncora and nearby Lobitos give warmer-water options on the north coast. The Peru place in the catalog is Cusco and the Andes. Best: Chicama about Apr–Oct (southern winter swell). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the surfing list in the old Catalog Wishlist (not yet imported).
grainNote: Two coasts about 800 km apart, joined under one old name.

name: Kauai
why: Hanalei Bay, a long right-hand reef point on the north shore, handles everything from small to large winter swell, and Poipu on the south shore picks up summer swell. A quieter, greener alternative to Oahu's crowds. Best: Winter swell on the north shore; summer on the south shore. (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the hiking list (same name).

name: Lombok & Sumbawa
why: Desert Point (Bangko-Bangko) is a legendary left barrel, with Ekas and a string of southern reefs along the way. Less developed than Bali, and a short hop east. Best: About May–Sep (dry season). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Near the diving list entry "Gili Islands & Lombok" (a different attraction).

name: El Salvador
why: Punta Roca, Sunzal and El Zonte are right-hand points and reefs along the La Libertad coast, close to the capital. Warm water, consistent swell and a growing surf-town scene. Best: About Apr–Oct (south swell). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the surfing list in the old Catalog Wishlist (not yet imported).

name: Pichilemu
why: Punta de Lobos is a big-wave point on the world big-wave tour, with the gentle left at La Puntilla for everyone else. A cold, uncrowded Pacific coast a few hours south of Santiago. Best: Swell most of the year; cold water, biggest in the southern winter. (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the surfing list in the old Catalog Wishlist (not yet imported).
grainNote: A surf town and its coast, one trip.

name: Siargao
why: Cloud 9 is the Philippines' best-known wave, a hollow right reef point, with a lively surf-town scene around General Luna. Palawan, the nearest catalog place, has only minor surf. Best: Sep–Nov (some years to March). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.)

name: Florianópolis
why: The island has dozens of surfable beaches, Joaquina and Praia Mole the best known, and a strong surf culture. Rio, the nearest catalog place, has city waves only. Best: Autumn and winter swells; warm summer water for beginners. (Established. Researched Oct 2026.)
grainNote: An island and its beaches, one trip.

name: Sayulita & the Riviera Nayarit
why: Sayulita's gentle waves are among Mexico's best learner spots, with Punta Mita and the Nayarit points nearby for more experienced surfers. The Pacific coast opposite Los Cabos. Best: About May–Oct (south swell). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.)
grainNote: A coast of small beach towns, one trip.
